artists.biography:
The Cure are an English alternative rock band formed in Crawley, West Sussex in 1976. The band has experienced several line-up changes, with frontman, vocalist, guitarist and principal songwriter Robert Smith being the only constant member. The Cure first began releasing music in the late 1970s with its debut album Three Imaginary Boys (1979); this, along with several early singles, placed the band as part of the post-punk and New Wave movements that had sprung up in the wake of the punk rock revolution in the United Kingdom. During the early 1980s, the band's increasingly dark and tormented music helped form the gothic rock genre.

After the release of Pornography (1982), the band's future was uncertain and Smith was keen to move past the gloomy reputation his band had acquired. With the 1982 single "Let's Go to Bed" Smith began to place a pop sensibility into the band's music (as well as a unique stage look). The Cure's popularity increased as the decade wore on, especially in the United States where the songs "Just Like Heaven", "Lovesong" and "Friday I'm in Love" entered the Billboard Hot 100 chart. By the start of the 1990s, The Cure were one of the most popular alternative rock bands in the world. The band is estimated to have sold 27 million albums as of 2004. The Cure have released thirteen studio albums, 10 EPs and over thirty singles during the course of their career. Since 2010, they have been working on a fourteenth studio album.

perplexity.description:
Standing On A Beach/Staring At The Sea: The Singles is a greatest hits compilation by The Cure, released in May 1986 on Fiction Records in the UK and Elektra Records in the US. The album marks a decade since the band's formation in 1976 and compiles their commercially released singles spanning from 1978 to 1985. The dual title derives from the opening lyrics of the band's debut single, "Killing an Arab," which opens the collection. The compilation was issued across multiple formats—vinyl, cassette, and CD—each with varying track selections and bonus material, with the CD edition retitled Staring At The Sea and featuring four additional non-single tracks that had received music video releases.

The album captures The Cure's evolution through their early post-punk and new wave period, presenting thirteen singles in chronological order on the vinyl edition. The tracklist encompasses the band's most recognizable material, including "Boys Don't Cry," "A Forest," "Let's Go to Bed," "The Walk," and "The Lovecats," showcasing their progression from darker, angular post-punk toward more accessible pop sensibilities. The cassette edition notably includes B-sides, offering a more comprehensive view of the band's output during this formative decade.

The compilation achieved significant commercial success, reaching number 4 on the UK charts and number 48 on the US charts, eventually earning RIAA certification as a 2X platinum record. Standing On A Beach/Staring At The Sea remains one of the most comprehensive early retrospectives of The Cure's singles era, serving as an effective entry point to their catalog while documenting their artistic development across their first eight years.
